The constraint we start with

What slows saas & startups teams down.

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

01

Product signals never reach sales or success

Signups, feature adoption and usage drops live in the product analytics tool, while account owners work from the CRM. Product-qualified accounts wait days for a reply, and a quiet decline in usage is noticed only when the renewal is lost.

02

Trials and renewals that feel like traps

Trial reminders are generic, renewal notices are missing and cancellation is hard to find. India's dark patterns guidelines name silent trial-to-paid conversion and hidden cancellation explicitly, so the billing journey needs honest notices as well as good conversion.

03

Failed payments quietly become churn

Renewals on India-issued cards and UPI run on e-mandates with bank pre-debit notices and extra authentication above set limits, so a failed renewal often needs the customer to act. Without a recovery flow, customers who wanted to stay lose access and finance chases them by hand.

04

Support volume grows faster than the team

Repeated setup questions bury urgent bugs and billing issues. A bot that answers from stale docs or never hands off makes things worse; one grounded in current docs, with a clear route to a person, frees the team for the hard cases.

05

Marketplaces depend on trust and liquidity

Supply applications pile up in spreadsheets, risky listings slip through and buyers wait without a match. Each queue needs rules, reviewers and response times, now including the grievance timelines in India's amended IT Rules.

06

AI features ship without a quality or cost baseline

Prompt and model changes go live on gut feel. Without evaluation sets, review queues and cost per task tracking, teams cannot tell whether a release made answers better, worse or only more expensive.

The perfect automation

Product-signal routing: from usage events to the right owner

One event spine connects product analytics to everyone who acts on it. Agreed value events in PostHog are scored against fit and usage rules; low-touch accounts get guidance tied to the step they missed, product-qualified accounts reach an account executive with context and a booking link, and accounts with falling usage reach customer success before renewal.

  1. 01

    Agree value events and instrument them

    Define the activation milestone, the product-qualified threshold and the risk signals with product and revenue owners, then instrument or clean up the events in PostHog with account-level grouping and an event specification versioned in GitHub.

    PPostHogGGitHub
  2. 02

    Score accounts on fit and usage

    A dbt model in BigQuery joins product usage with CRM firmographics and Stripe plan data to give every account a fit score, a usage score and a reason code. Scores refresh nightly, and high-intent events such as a demo request trigger routing immediately.

    GBGoogle BigQueryddbtSStripeHHubSpot
  3. 03

    Route each account to one next step

    n8n sends low-touch accounts an in-product tip or email for the step they missed, creates a HubSpot or Salesforce task for product-qualified accounts, and raises a renewal-risk alert for customer success. Each account follows one route at a time.

    nn8nRResendHHubSpotSSalesforce
  4. 04

    Brief the owner instead of messaging for them

    An AI-drafted brief in Slack summarizes what the account did, which features it used, open tickets and suggested questions, with links to the source records. The owner decides whether and how to reach out.

    OOpenAISSlack
  5. 05

    Close the loop and recalibrate

    Owners log outcomes in the CRM. A weekly review compares routed accounts with a holdout group where volumes allow and adjusts thresholds, messages and owner capacity before the routing expands to more segments.

    HHubSpotMPMicrosoft Power BIPPostHog

Human checkpoint

Account executives and customer success managers decide every outreach, offer and discount. Revenue operations and the product lead approve scoring rules and message copy. Onboarding tips run within those rules; no sales message is sent automatically, and personal-email signups reach sales only on request.

What changes

  • Product-qualified accounts reach a named owner while they are still evaluating.
  • Customer success hears about falling usage before the renewal conversation, not after it.
  • Self-serve users get guidance tied to the step they missed instead of a generic drip.
  • Product, sales and success share one definition of activation, qualification and risk.

Automation playbook

Start where the work repeats.

A selection from the playbook. Each blueprint shows the trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Discover & evaluate · 3–5 weeks

Product-qualified lead and demo routing

Demo requests and trial accounts that cross agreed usage and fit thresholds reach the right account executive with a usage brief and a booking link, while low-fit signups stay in self-serve journeys.

View the blueprint ↗Sign up & activate · 3–4 weeks

Event-driven onboarding and activation journeys

In-product tips, email, push and opt-in WhatsApp messages triggered by what each new user or workspace has and has not done, stopping the moment the activation milestone is reached.

View the blueprint ↗Sign up & activate · 5–7 weeks

Supply-side onboarding and verification queue

Seller, provider or host applications are collected in one structured flow, checked automatically where a reliable source exists, and decided by a reviewer working from a checklist in a single queue.

View the blueprint ↗Convert & pay · 2–4 weeks

Trial-to-paid nudges with clear renewal notices

Trial reminders tailored to what each account actually used, stating the conversion date, the price including any GST and the cancellation route plainly, with high-fit trials flagged to sales.

View the blueprint ↗Use, match & get help · 3–5 weeks

Two-sided matching alerts

New demand is matched against providers' saved criteria and availability, the best-fit providers are notified on the channel they chose, and operations steps in when a request stays unfilled.

View the blueprint ↗Use, match & get help · 5–8 weeks

Trust and safety moderation queue

Listings, reviews, profiles and messages are screened with rules and a moderation model, risky items are held for trained moderators, and every decision, notice and appeal is recorded with a policy reason.

How we work

A clear delivery rhythm, from discovery to daily operation.

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 01 · 1–2 weeksDiscover

    We map the user and customer journey from signup to renewal with the founder and the product, revenue and support leads, audit the event taxonomy, billing setup and CRM hygiene, and trace where personal data flows. We then pick one workflow where a clear signal already exists and an owner is ready to act on it.

  2. 02 · 1–2 weeksDesign

    We specify events, scoring rules, message matrices, review queues and escalation paths, and write down every human checkpoint and stop condition. For AI features we agree the evaluation rubric, confidence thresholds and disclosure wording before anything is built.

  3. 03 · 2–4 weeksBuild

    We build in your accounts: n8n workflows, PostHog destinations, CRM objects, Retool queues, retrieval indexes and dashboards, starting in Stripe test mode and CRM sandboxes. Every workflow gets logging, failure alerts and a feature-flag kill switch.

  4. 04 · 1–2 weeksValidate & launch

    We test with seeded accounts and replayed events, run AI features in shadow mode where drafts are reviewed but not sent, keep a holdout group for nudges, and release behind feature flags to a first segment before widening.

  5. 05 · Monthly, ongoingOperate & improve

    We watch failures and queue ages, compare KPIs with the baseline and holdout each month, tune thresholds and messages, refresh knowledge sources and evaluation sets, and review access and data retention every quarter.

Suggested first pilot

Product-signal routing pilot

A pilot of four to six weeks on one segment: one activation milestone with stuck-step messages, one product-qualified rule routed to account executives with a brief, and one renewal-risk alert for customer success. We agree a baseline first, with a holdout group where volumes allow, so the result is judged on your own numbers rather than on estimates.

  • Event taxonomy cleanup for the activation path in PostHog
  • Stuck-step messages by email and in-product, with caps and stop rules
  • One product-qualified rule creating CRM tasks with Slack briefs
  • One weekly renewal-risk alert for customer success
  • Baseline, holdout group and a weekly calibration session

Measures

Know whether it is working.

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

Activation rate

Share of new accounts or workspaces that reach the agreed value milestone within the agreed window after signup.

Product-qualified account to opportunity rate

Share of accounts routed as product-qualified that become sales opportunities within the agreed period.

Speed to first meaningful response

Elapsed time from a demo request or product-qualified signal to the first relevant contact by the assigned owner.

Trial-to-paid conversion

Share of trial accounts in a start cohort that become paying accounts by an agreed deadline after the trial ends.
